messages.content: I see a login from a location I don't recognize. What should I do?

I've checked your account activity. There was a login on November 14th from Seattle, WA on an unrecognized Windows PC — this device has never been associated with your account before.

Here's what I recommend:
1. **Change your password immediately** — I can walk you through this.
2. **Enable two-factor authentication** if you haven't already.
3. **Revoke the unrecognized device** — I can do this now with your confirmation.

Would you like me to revoke access for that Seattle device? I'll need you to confirm with your account email first.
Show me all devices that have accessed my account in the last 30 days.

Here are all 3 devices that accessed your account in the last 30 days:

| Device | OS | Location | Last Login | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 15 Pro | iOS 17 | Boston, MA | Nov 20 | ✅ Recognized |
| MacBook Pro | macOS 14 | Boston, MA | Nov 18 | ✅ Recognized |
| Unknown Windows PC | Windows 11 | Seattle, WA | Nov 14 | ⚠️ Unrecognized |

The Windows PC in Seattle is flagged as unrecognized. I recommend revoking its access. Shall I proceed?
I'm locked out of my Peloton account after entering the wrong password too many times.

No problem — I can help you regain access securely. Here's how the process works:

1. I'll send a one-time verification code (OTP) to your registered email address.
2. You'll enter that code to verify your identity.
3. Once verified, you'll be prompted to set a new password.

Could you confirm the email address on your account so I can send the code? I'll mask it for privacy once you provide it.
I entered the OTP code but it says it's invalid.

OTP codes expire after 10 minutes and are single-use. A few things to check:
- Make sure you're using the most recent code (check that you didn't accidentally use an older email).
- Confirm there are no extra spaces when entering the code.

I can send you a fresh OTP right now. Would you like me to resend it to your registered email? Note: after 3 failed attempts, the account will require manual verification with our support team for security purposes.
What's the difference between All-Access Membership and Peloton App+?

Here's a direct comparison:

| Feature | All-Access ($44/mo) | Peloton App+ ($24/mo) |
|---|---|---|
| Live classes | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| On-demand classes | ✅ Unlimited | ✅ Unlimited |
| User profiles | Up to 2 | 1 |
| Leaderboard | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Works without equipment | ❌ Requires Peloton gear | ✅ Any device/gym equipment |
| Performance tracking | Full | Basic |
| Price | $44/month | $24/month |

**Recommendation:** If you own Peloton equipment and use live classes, All-Access is worth it. If you primarily use the app on a phone or gym treadmill, App+ saves you $240/year.
I only use the Peloton app on my phone — no equipment. Is All-Access worth it for me?

Based on your usage pattern (app-only, no Peloton equipment), the Peloton App+ tier at $24/month would be a better fit and save you $240 per year. You'd retain access to the full on-demand class library including cycling, running, yoga, strength, and meditation. The main things you'd lose vs. All-Access are: live classes, the leaderboard, and the ability to add a second user profile. If those features aren't part of your routine, App+ provides equal value at a lower cost. Would you like a link to manage your subscription?
